nyc-outdoor-dining.notes: Requires an NYC.ID account. Fees: license $1,050 (once per 4-year term), public hearing $500-$900 for roadway, refundable security deposit $2,500 roadway / $1,500 sidewalk, plus an annual revocable consent fee by sector and size (sector 1-4: sidewalk $6/$10/$18/$31 per sq ft; seasonal roadway $5/$8/$14/$25). Review can take 6 months. Eligibility: ground floor, street-visible, directly accessible, with a DOHMH food service establishment permit. Seasonal roadway cafes operate Apr 1-Nov 29; year-round roadway applications open early September 2026. The temporary Open Restaurants program no longer accepts applications. Questions: diningoutnyc@dot.nyc.gov.

chi-sidewalk-cafe.notes: Permit term March 1 through end of February, renewable annually (renewals open now). Payment via the portal after approval; BACP notifies electronically. The permit and approved plan must be printed and displayed at the main entrance. 'A full list of required materials can be found on the portal.' Questions: publicwayuse@cityofchicago.org. Cafe must be on the sidewalk only, fully bounded, with 6 ft pedestrian clearance. Fee not stated on the page. Rules: chicago.gov Sidewalk Cafe Rules and Regulations (not read).

lv-building.notes: Apply at lasvegasnevada.gov/Dashboard ('Apply for a permit requiring plans', Google Chrome required); $55 admin fee to enter the review queue. 'Effective January 1, 2020, all NEW commercial, residential, and civil building plans MUST be submitted electronically.' 'Only a Nevada licensed contractor may obtain a building permit for commercial construction.' Incomplete applications are not accepted; permits expire 180 days after issuance with no passed inspection. Express plan review: $550 admin + $660/hr. The city also publishes a Food-Service-Establishment-Guideline.pdf and Tenant-Improvement-Guideline.pdf (not read). Fax (702) 382-1240 appears on the instructions header but is not stated as accepting applications.
